entries.title: Job 39:1
segments: Wild goats of the rock--hinds; those that live in the mountains, far away from the abodes of men.

entries.title: Job 39:3
segments:
They bring forth their young; dependent only on the care of God. 
 
Creatures that are dependent only on the providence of God, are by him provided for, as really as those whose wants are supplied by human instrumentality; while in both he equally shows his wisdom, power, and love.

entries.title: Job 39:4
segments: With corn; or, in the open field; that is, far away from all human care.

entries.title: Job 39:7
segments: Neither regardeth; literally, heareth not.  He is far removed from the driver.

entries.title: Job 39:9
segments: Unicorn; according to some, the eastern buffalo; according to others, the rhinoceros, an immensely strong animal with one horn a little above its nose, or some other wild animal of great strength. See note to

. 
 
It is not enough for usefulness to have great strength, or superior natural qualities; there must also be the ability and the disposition rightly to use them.

entries.title: Job 39:13
segments: Gavest thou--the ostrich? the exact rendering of this verse is difficult.  Some propose to translate as follows: "The wing of the ostriches exulteth: are its plumage and feathers those of the stork?" meaning, does the ostrich have the tender dispositon of a stork towards its young?

entries.title: Job 39:16
segments:
She is hardened against her young; treats her young as if she had no natural affection. 
 
To all classes of creatures God gives just the kind and degree of wisdom which they need to accomplish the ends for which he made them; what would only be a useless annoyance to them, he has wisely and mercifully withheld.

entries.title: Job 39:18
segments: She lifteth up herself; to escape her pursuers, running by the help of her wings with great swiftness.

entries.title: Job 39:19
segments: The courage, agility, and strength of the horse, his affection and docility, his readiness to labor, his patience even under hardship and abuse, and his subserviency to the various wants of men, are all evidence of the goodness of God, in which his hand should be gratefully recognized.

entries.title: Job 39:20
segments: Canst thou make him afraid? or, cause him to leap.  Is it from thee that he receives the agility of a locust in leaping?

entries.title: Job 39:24
segments: Neither believeth he; that is, for joy.  But many prefer to render, "neither will he stand still when there is the sound of the trumpet."

entries.title: Job 39:30
segments: The most rapacious and savage of the feathered tribes, who teach their young to revel in blood, do not take the life of their own species; this is the sin of the abused understandings and depraved hearts and bloody hands of men.
